title: Mean and first-level weight of a subcube
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be nonempty, and let $b\in\{0,1\}^n$. Define $q(x)=1$ when $x_i=b_i$ for every $i\in J$ and $q(x)=0$ otherwise. Under the uniform measure on the Boolean cube, its expectation and first-level Fourier weight satisfy $\mathbb E[q]=2^{-|J|}$ and $W_1[q]=|J|/2^{2|J|}$.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number
The assignment $b$ is a Boolean vector of dimension $n$
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be nonempty, let $b\in\{0,1\}^n$, and put $k=|J|$ and $q(x)=\mathbf 1_{\{x_i=b_i\ \text{for every }i\in J\}}$ for $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
Using uniform expectation $\mathbb E[h]=2^{-n}\sum_xh(x)$, singleton Fourier coefficients $\widehat q(\{i\})=\mathbb E[q(x)(-1)^{x_i}]$, and degree-one Fourier weight $W^1[q]=\sum_{i<n}\widehat q(\{i\})^2$, one has
\[
\mathbb E[q]=\frac{1}{2^k}
\quad\text{and}\quad
W^1[q]=\frac{k}{2^{2k}}.
\]
